The bot account [[User:WoWBot|WoWBot]] keeps the game data on this wiki current. After each Steam update of Erenshor, it reads the game files and updates the pages that show game data. This page explains which pages the bot maintains, what you can change on them, and how to report a wrong value.

The game data on this wiki comes from Erenshor {{#invoke:Erenshor/Build|text}}.

For everything else about editing this wiki, see the [[Erenshor Wiki:Community Portal|community portal]].

== How game data reaches the wiki ==
After a game update:
# An export tool reads the game files and writes their data to a database. Some rules exist only in the game code, for example the chances of world drops. The export reads them from the code.
# The bot makes article text and Lua data modules from the database.
# The bot writes a page only when its text changed. It does not write a page that someone edited after the bot read it. It does not write a page whose new text shows a script error.

The same database feeds the [https://erenshor.compendiums.org interactive map]. The export tool and the bot are open source: [https://github.com/glockyco/erenshor-data-mining erenshor-data-mining].

== Who maintains which pages ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Pages !! Maintained by !! What this means for you
|-
| Data modules under <code>Module:Erenshor/Data/</code> || the bot || Do not edit them. The next update replaces them.
|-
| The other [[Special:PrefixIndex/Module:Erenshor/|modules under <code>Module:Erenshor/</code>]], and the templates listed below || the project || Ask for a change on the [[Erenshor Wiki talk:Game Data|talk page]]. An edit on the wiki stops the next update of that page until the change is copied into the project.
|-
| Item, character, ability, stance, and zone articles, and the overview tables on [[Weapons]] and [[Armor]] || the bot and you || The bot writes the infobox data and the overview tables. You write everything else. See the next section.
|-
| All other pages, for example guides, quests, classes, factions, lore, mechanics, and the main page || you || The bot does not edit them.
|}

== Editing an article that the bot maintains ==
When the bot updates an article, it keeps all text outside the infoboxes. It also keeps each infobox that it does not make itself, for example a chest infobox that an editor added to a boss page. The update does not touch the "Store inventory" tables on vendor pages. <code><nowiki>{{Vendor stock}}</nowiki></code> shows a vendor's stock from the game data.

In an infobox that the bot makes, the bot replaces each field with the game data, except for the fields in this table.

{| class="wikitable"
! Infobox !! Field !! Your value
|-
| Item || <code>othersource</code> || Kept
|-
| Item || <code>type</code> || Merged
|-
| Item || <code>questsource</code> || Merged
|-
| Item || <code>relatedquest</code> || Merged
|-
| Character || <code>imagecaption</code> || Kept
|-
| Character || <code>location</code> || Kept
|-
| Character || <code>zones</code> || Replaced, kept when the game has no value
|-
| Character || <code>coordinates</code> || Replaced, kept when the game has no value
|-
| Character || <code>respawn</code> || Replaced, kept when the game has no value
|-
| Stance || <code>imagecaption</code> || Kept
|-
| Zone || <code>image</code> || Kept, filled when blank
|-
| Zone || <code>imagecaption</code> || Kept, filled when blank
|-
| Zone || <code>level</code> || Kept, filled when blank
|-
| Zone || <code>type</code> || Kept, filled when blank
|-
| Zone || <code>maplink</code> || Kept, filled when blank
|-
| Zone || <code>connects</code> || Kept, filled when blank
|}

* '''Kept''': the bot does not change your value.
* '''Kept, filled when blank''': the bot keeps your value. When the field is blank, the bot fills it from the game data.
* '''Replaced, kept when the game has no value''': the game data replaces your value. When the game data has no value, the bot keeps yours.
* '''Merged''': the field is a list. The bot adds its entries. When one of your entries links the same page as a bot entry, the bot entry replaces it. Your other entries stay.

On character pages, the type (Boss, Elite, Enemy, NPC, or Chest) comes from the game data. To correct a type, report it.

Each infobox that the bot makes has a <code>stablekey</code>. The key ties the infobox to one thing in the game, for example to one of several variants with the same name. Do not change or remove it.

== Data-backed item pages ==
Pages using [[Template:ItemData|ItemData]] read their item values from the game data. A data update does not rewrite the surrounding article text. Keep the call's <code>stablekey</code> unchanged, because it identifies the exact item variant.

These fields belong to editors and remain unchanged:
{| class="wikitable"
! Template !! Field !! Your value
|-
| ItemData || <code>type</code> || Kept
|-
| ItemData || <code>questsource</code> || Kept
|-
| ItemData || <code>relatedquest</code> || Kept
|-
| ItemData || <code>othersource</code> || Kept
|}

Put strategy and other prose outside the call. Report incorrect game values instead of adding stat or source overrides.

Use [[Template:ItemData/SourceNote|ItemData/SourceNote]] for an editor's source note whose item and source identities are known. When the data covers that source, compare the note with the displayed source and remove only redundant text. Leave other notes unchanged until reviewed.

* [[:Category:Item data calls with invalid identities]] means the call needs the correct item key.
* [[:Category:Item data calls with unsupported parameters]] means a parameter is not an editor field. Preserve its useful text outside the call and report any missing game data.
* [[:Category:Item data notes covered by game data]] identifies source notes ready for review.

== When the game data is wrong or missing ==
Do not correct a value that the bot writes. The next update replaces your correction. Report the value instead. The fix then goes into the export, so that every page and the interactive map show the correct value.

{| class="wikitable"
! What you found !! What to do
|-
| A wrong value, for example a wrong drop chance || Report it.
|-
| Something that the game does but the data does not show, for example a scripted spawn || Report it. The export can usually read it from the game code.
|-
| A wrong name or type, or two things that the data mixes up || Report it. The export corrects these in its mapping file.
|-
| A source of an item that the data does not list || Write it in the item's <code>othersource</code> field, and report it.
|-
| Strategy, notes, and explanations || Write them in the article text.
|}

=== How to report ===
Write in the <code>#wiki-chat</code> channel of the [https://discord.gg/DxqZc5Dc9q Erenshor Discord], or on the [[Erenshor Wiki talk:Game Data|talk page]] of this page. Name the page, the field, and what the game shows. A screenshot helps.

== Removed, renamed, and unused content ==
When a game update removes or renames something, its page stays on the wiki. Older links still lead to it, and readers can see what changed. A box from [[Template:Historical Content|Historical Content]] at the top of the page tells readers what happened.

{| class="wikitable"
! What happened !! What the page shows
|-
| The game no longer has it || A box says that it is no longer in the game. When the patch notes name the update, the box links them. The page is in [[:Category:Removed Content]].
|-
| It is still in the game, but players can no longer get it || A box says that it can no longer be obtained. The page is in [[:Category:Unobtainable Content]].
|-
| It is in the game files, but nothing in the game spawns it || A box says this. If simulated players can still name it in chat, the box says that too. The page is in [[:Category:Unused Content]].
|-
| The game renamed it, or simulated players call it by another name || The other name redirects to the page with the current name.
|-
| The game now has several versions of it || The page under the old title links each version.
|}

The bot adds these boxes, redirects, and links from a list that the project keeps. To add a page to the list, [[#How to report|report it]] and name your source, for example the patch notes. On a page that the bot does not maintain, for example a quest, you can also add the box yourself.

Do not delete these pages.

== Links and tooltips ==
Links to items, characters, abilities, quests, zones, factions, and classes use link templates. A link template shows the name with an icon. When you move the pointer over the link, a card shows the in-game tooltip.

* To link a page by its name, write for example <code><nowiki>{{ItemLink|Ember Longsword}}</nowiki></code>.
* Things that share a page and an icon need no key. Give the link a <code>stablekey</code> when their icons differ, or when several abilities share the page, because ability tooltips need an exact identity.
* In the source editor, the '''Erenshor link''' button in the ''Insert'' group finds the correct template and key for you.

The tooltip templates show the in-game tooltip on a page: [[Template:ItemTooltip|ItemTooltip]], [[Template:SpellTooltip|SpellTooltip]], [[Template:SkillTooltip|SkillTooltip]], and [[Template:StanceTooltip|StanceTooltip]].

== Data-backed lists and quest panels ==
Place a view template on a page to show a list from the game data. It changes after a data update without replacing the surrounding article text. Keep strategy and editor-written sub-area notes outside the template.

{| class="wikitable"
! View !! Data module !! Use
|-
| [[Template:Vendor stock|Vendor stock]] || [[Module:Erenshor/Data/VendorStock]] || A vendor's items, prices, and unlock conditions
|-
| [[Template:Zone roster|Zone roster]] || [[Module:Erenshor/Data/ZoneRosters]] || A zone's characters by encounter tier, with level ranges and spawn conditions
|-
| [[Template:Class abilities|Class abilities]] || [[Module:Erenshor/Data/ClassAbilities]] || The spells and skills taught by obtainable items, with class-specific required levels and alternative teaching items
|-
| [[Template:Quest data|Quest data]] || [[Module:Erenshor/Data/Quests]] || A quest's acquisition and completion routes, requirements, rewards, and alternatives
|-
| [[Template:Game board|Game board]] || [[Module:Erenshor/Data/GameBoard]] || The Braxonian Game Board's bosses, pieces, levels, and drops
|-
| [[Template:World drops|World drops]] || [[Module:Erenshor/Data/WorldDrops]] || Special world drop rolls on eligible loot-bearing kills
|}

For example, write <code><nowiki>{{Zone roster}}</nowiki></code> on a zone page, or <code><nowiki>{{Class abilities|stablekey=class:druid}}</nowiki></code> to select a class explicitly. An entity-specific view without a key uses the entity of its kind on the current page. If several entities share that page, give the template the intended <code>stablekey</code>. Use <code><nowiki>{{Game board}}</nowiki></code> for the board's boss table.

Spawn chances are chances per eligible spawn roll, not the chance of meeting a character anywhere in a zone. Scripted encounters do not imply a fixed spawn position. Furniture-only rows require the named set to be placed.

=== Reading data in your own module ===
Each data module's opening comment describes its fields and their types. Use [[Module:Erenshor/Link]] for article-backed identities so links and tooltips follow [[Module:Erenshor/Data/Links]]. Some fields carry native references with a name and an optional page. Preserve those references instead of guessing a page for an entity without an article. For example:

<syntaxhighlight lang="lua">
local data = mw.loadData("Module:Erenshor/Data/ClassAbilities")
local Link = require("Module:Erenshor/Link")
local p = {}
function p.example()
    local out = {}
    for _, row in ipairs(data["class:druid"] or {}) do
        table.insert(out, Link.render({ kind = "ability", stablekey = row.ability }))
    end
    return table.concat(out, "<br>")
end
return p
</syntaxhighlight>

For identities on the current page, call <code>Link.pageKeys(kind, page)</code>. It reads the compact [[Module:Erenshor/Data/PageKeys]] index without loading the full link catalog.

Your own module is editor-maintained. Do not edit a generated data page to add a missing fact, because the next update replaces it. [[#How to report|Report the missing fact]] so the export and every view can use the correction.

== Images ==
Every picture's file name says what it shows and whose it is: the name of its subject, then its role.
{| class="wikitable"
! File name !! Shows !! Uploaded by
|-
| <code>Copper Sword icon.png</code> || The game's icon of an item, spell, skill, or stance || The bot, from the game's files after each game update
|-
| <code>Faith render.png</code> || A character or an item rendered from the game's 3D model, alone on a transparent background || The bot, after a person reviewed the picture
|-
| <code>Wolfhide Boots render (male).png</code> || An item worn on the male or the female body, where the two differ || The bot, after a person reviewed the picture
|-
| <code>Faith screenshot.png</code> || A character or an item in the game, as a player sees it || Editors
|-
| <code>Shrine of Blessings interface.png</code> || A window of the game that something opens, such as a shrine's or a vendor's || Editors
|}
The subject is the name in the game without the characters that file names cannot hold, such as colons: the icon of ''Stance: Aggressive'' is <code>Stance Aggressive icon.png</code>. Older names, such as <code>Faith.png</code>, redirect to the file that took their place, so old links keep working, but new pages should use the names above.

Icons carry no frame: [[Template:Icon]] draws items in a slot with a blue gradient ring and spells, skills, and stances in a black border, so use it to show an icon in your own text. Large infobox pictures show without a frame. Each picture has one file. When several items, spells, or skills share a picture, every other name redirects to that file, so a game update changes it once. When a game update renames something, the bot moves its file to the new name with its history and leaves a redirect behind.

A character infobox shows the render first and the screenshot as a second tab, labelled Render and Screenshot. A character with only one of the two shows it alone. The infobox names both files, so you can see the name to use in its source.

An item infobox shows the item's render, or its male and female renders, then its screenshot, as tabs labelled Render, Male, Female, and Screenshot. An item with none of these files shows its icon, and tooltips and item links always show the icon. Consumables, scrolls, rings, and other items without a model have no render. The item infobox also names its screenshot file.

An interface picture belongs in the article's text; the infobox shows only renders, screenshots, and icons.

* To add or improve a screenshot, upload it under the screenshot name that its infobox names, such as <code>Faith screenshot.png</code> or <code>Copper Sword screenshot.png</code>. The tab appears once the page is refreshed. The bot never uploads to, moves, or deletes a screenshot.
* The bot changes an icon or render only when WoWBot or [[User:WoWMuch|WoWMuch]], who runs it, uploaded the latest version, so an upload of yours always stays.
* Zone pictures belong to the editors. The bot does not render or upload them.

== For administrators ==
* WoWBot is a bot account of [[User:WoWMuch|WoWMuch]]. Its edits are marked as bot edits.
* When a bot edit is wrong, undo it and report it. The bot writes a page only when nobody changed it after the bot read it, so the next update starts from your version.
